title: Data controls intake scorecard and response procedures for PII & log requests
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: create a pragmatic intake scorecard and set of response procedures aimed at non-bug customer requests related to data controls: logging redaction, retention adjustments, PII handling, and audit exports. Goal is to reduce time-to-resolution for enterprise requests, improve routing accuracy, and ensure consistent legal/security review while preserving observability. This ticket will produce: 1) a numeric scorecard template (0-100) with factor weights and examples; 2) a routing matrix mapping score ranges to owning teams and SLA classes; 3) templated response playbooks for the most common request types (redaction, retention change, PII deletion, audit export); 4) a short training checklist and sample Confluence pages for support/SEs. Scope: covers customer-initiated non-bug requests only. Out of scope: incident remediation, security vulnerabilities, and system-level policy changes that must go through ENG RFC flow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scorecard template published in Confluence with weight rationale and 5 example scored requests.
- Routing matrix implemented as a triage form integration (Zendesk/Intercom) and validated in two pilot accounts.
- Playbooks for redaction, retention change, PII handling, and audit export created, each with step-by-step engineering tasks, legal sign-offs, and checklist.
- SLAs defined and agreed with Legal, Security, and Solutions Eng; internal run-through completed with SEs.
- Hand-off checklist and training doc available for Support and SEs.
success_metrics:
- Median time from intake to an approved routing decision <= 24 hours for high impact requests.
- Median end-to-end time to resolution for high-priority requests reduced by 40% in pilot accounts within 6 weeks.
- >90% of requests correctly routed on first decision during pilot.
- Number of ad-hoc reassignments decreases by 50% vs current baseline.
proposed_workflow_summary: 1) Customer fills standardized intake form (required fields include sample log snippet, retention/PII request details, compliance rationale). 2) System computes score via scorecard factors. 3) Request routed by score range and label to specific team queue (SE + PM / Enterprise SRE + Legal / Support handbook). 4) Owner performs required artifact collection and raises legal/security review where indicated. 5) Implementation planned with target window per SLA; release note and audit trail recorded. 6) Post-implementation confirmation and customer closeout + retro if escalation occurred.
scorecard_factors: Scope of data affected (single org vs multi-tenant) - weight 15
Likelihood of production impact / feature break - weight 10
initial_routing_rules: Score >= 85: Immediate Enterprise SRE + Legal + Security involvement; target implementation window 3 business days; PM owns customer comms.
65 <= Score < 85: PM + Solutions Eng lead; security review if PII sensitivity >= 20; target implementation 7-14 business days.
40 <= Score < 65: PM review + Support templated workflow; SE consult on necessary engineering work; implementation timeline depends on capacity but <30 days target.
Score < 40: Support handles via knowledge base / standard process; automated guidance and no engineering change unless escalated.
All audit export requests require a legal & security checklist regardless of score; certain exports must follow export control rules and be logged in central audit registry.
recommended_SLA:
Acknowledgement: High (score>=85) within 4 business hours; Medium (65-84) within 24 business hours; Low (<65) within 3 business days.
Decision (routing + next steps): High within 24 hours; Medium within 72 hours; Low within 7 days.
Target implementation: High 3 business days; Medium 7-14 business days; Low 30 days or as per backlog.
Escalation path: If target window cannot be met, auto-escalate to PM Director and notify customer with proposed timeline within 24 hours of escalation.
required_artifacts: Customer intake form (template) - must include sample log snippet or schema
Example redaction PR with checklist for release notes
Legal sign-off template for PII retention/deletion changes
Runbook for applying retention policy changes in production
open_questions: Should the scorecard be strictly numeric or allow category overrides by PMs/Legal?
What level of sample data is acceptable in the intake form (raw logs vs redacted examples)?
How do we surface retrospective cost estimates for implementation in the ticket to inform customer expectations?
Do we require a signed DPA amendment for retention length increases beyond contract?
Which data residency constraints automatically force Private deployment review?
